descriptionChirho: Physically disabled in the feet or legs, unable to walk normally; used of persons who are crippled or hobble. Greek χωλός describes a permanent or chronic physical disability. Multilingual evidence is uniform across both clusters: eng 'lame,' spa 'cojo(s),' hin लंगड़ा/लंगड़े (laṅgṛā, crippled), arb أَعْرَجَ/عُرجٌ (aʿraj, lame), kor 절름발이 (jeolleumbal-i), swa 'kiwete/viwete' (crippled person/s). The split is purely grammatical: plural forms (S79113) vs singular forms (S79114) with identical meaning.
